record.paper_title: Statements and open problems on decidable sets X ⊆ N that contain informal notions and refer to the current knowledge on X
record.context_brief: Existence of a set meeting Conditions (1)–(5)
record.original_question: Does there exist a decidable set X ⊆ N such that all five of the paper's Conditions (1)–(5) hold simultaneously? Here Condition (1) says that a known algorithm with no input returns an integer n such that, if X is finite, then every element of X is at most n. Condition (2) says that there is a known algorithm deciding, for every k ∈ N, whether k ∈ X. Condition (3) says that no known algorithm with no input returns the truth value of the statement that X is infinite. Condition (4) says that X has many known elements and it is conjectured, but not yet proved, that X is infinite. Condition (5) says that X is naturally defined, the infiniteness of X is false or unproven, and among known sets Y ⊆ N with the same known elements, X has the simplest definition.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Is there a set X ⊆ N which satisfies Conditions (1)-(5)?

Definition 1.2. Conditions (1)-(5) concern sets X ⊆ N.
(1) A known algorithm with no input returns an integer n satisfying card(X) < ω ⇒ X ⊆ (−∞, n].
(2) A known algorithm for every k ∈ N decides whether or not k ∈ X.
(3) No known algorithm with no input returns the logical value of the statement card(X) = ω.
(4) There are many elements of X and it is conjectured, though so far unproven, that X is infinite.
(5) X is naturally defined. The infiniteness is false or unproven. X has the simplest definition among known sets Y ⊆ N with the same set of known elements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Informal setup. Consider subsets X ⊆ ℕ. For such a set, formulate the following five conditions, where the words "known" and "naturally defined" refer to the present state of mathematical knowledge:

(1) There is a known algorithm that, with no input, returns an integer n such that, if X is finite, then every element of X is ≤ n.
(2) There is a known algorithm that, for every k ∈ ℕ, decides whether k ∈ X.
(3) No currently known algorithm with no input returns the truth value of the statement "X is infinite."
(4) Many elements of X are known, and it is conjectured but not yet proved that X is infinite.
(5) X is naturally defined; the statement that X is infinite is either false or unproven; and among all currently known sets Y ⊆ ℕ that have the same set of currently known elements as X, the set X admits the simplest definition.

Question. Does there exist a decidable set X ⊆ ℕ for which Conditions (1)–(5) all hold simultaneously?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as Open Problem 1 in the Kozdęba–Tyszka work and reiterated in subsequent preprints by the same authors (2022–2023). No published resolution has been located; partial discussions involve candidate sets such as primes of the form n²+1 (linked to Landau's conjecture), where Conditions (2)–(5) are argued to hold but Condition (1) is conditional on an unproved hypothesis. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work by the same authors continues to treat Conditions (1)-(5) as unresolved.
